newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES SLIP LOWER IN PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES SLIP LOWER IN PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Istanbul shares eased in profit-taking on Monday after testing stiff resistance at the index's 70,000 level in an early rise that continued from last week, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at 69,186.72, down 307.31 points, or 0.44 percent from Friday. It sank to a low of 68,932 in the afternon from an early high of 70,154.
The index had soared 7.3 percent last week in an uptrend fuelled by limited cash influx and positive sentiment.
Trade volume dropped to 12.14 trillion lira from Friday's 13 trillion lira.

"An easing was expected this week after last week's sharp and non-stop rise. The index may first establish firm support at 67,500 to gain enough momentum to break the 70,000 barrier in a more healthy rise," said Hakan Tezcan from Korfezbank.
Brokers said selective activity continued and sentiment remained positive amid hopes of speedier privatisation and news of witholding tax to be imposed on Treasury bill and bonds.
The government is preparing a decree to impose a 10 percent witholding tax on interest income from bill and bond issues as part of the second revenue-raising package unveiled last week.

The tax will go into effect when the decree is published in the official gazette and will not be retroactive. The market hopes it may reduce attractiveness of state papers and divert some funds into the bourse.
The 85-share industrial index firmed 0.28 percent to 75,936.08 while the 15-share financial index shed 2.23 percent to 61,211.77. Of the 224 issues traded, 97 fell, 69 rose and 58 finished stable.

Utility Aktas Elektrik which gained 4,500 lira to 54,000 made up 19.3 percent of the total turnover. It was followed by largely state owned Turkish Airlines, up 3,000 lira at 30,000 and 00 and flat steel giant Eregli, steady at 10,000 lira.
